23	> **Preface:** "Orra Keddie was born in **1866** and married **Ansel Keddie in 1889**. He was
24	> **tester and separator man** at the Ostrey Hollow skimming station of the Larrow Valley Cooperative
25	> Creamery Association, and **kept its books in his own hand for twenty-nine seasons**. She began the
26	> diary in the **spring of 1897** and closed it in **1930**, and it was kept in **three ruled
27	> notebooks bought at Ashlin**. **The pages covering her girlhood and her family before 1889 were not
28	> preserved; nothing in her hand survives from before the marriage.** She writes **A.** for her
29	> husband throughout. A single later leaf, written in **1934** and laid loose inside the back cover of
30	> the third book, is printed at the end… nothing has been added and nothing altered but the spelling
31	> of two place names."
32	
33	**Why decisive:** she is the tester's wife AND the largest patron's sister — the exact junction of the
34	two families the affair turns on — **and she writes on the day, not in recollection.** Every other
35	narrator except Strawn's field notes (r06) and the Ammon invoice (r20) writes years or decades later.
36	**On any date or event she records at the time, r24 outranks every later memory, including Duncan's
37	(r18) and Hazel's (r17).** Limits: **no test figures, no averages, no money, and not the award** (the
38	editor notes the award is simply absent). It cannot touch Section C. **1926 has several leaves torn
39	out**; the editor did not try to supply them.

41	### 0.1 C1 — the Ostrey Hollow arithmetic. CLOSED except the price.
42	
43	**(a) The proportion, from the glassware.** The station's milk-test pipettes were blown to deliver
44	**17.6 c.c.** (Ammon & Sons invoice, 14 April 1897, specifies "17.6 c.c."; the test bottles were
45	"**8 per cent neck**," ruled to read 8 per cent *for that one charge and no other*). Ivy Keddie
46	measured the **nine** surviving pipettes against a calibrated burette at Farland on **9 March 1958**,
47	five runs each: mean **16.72 c.c.** — short **0.88 c.c.**
48	**16.72 ÷ 17.6 = 0.95 exactly.** The glass delivered **95 hundredths of its mark**, so every test made
49	on it was low **by one part in twenty (5 per cent), proportionally, not by fixed points.**
50	**recorded = true × 0.95.**
51	*Reject r19's "eleven pipettes … average 16.27 c.c."* — 16.27 ÷ 17.6 = 0.9244, which reproduces
52	nothing; 16.72 reproduces everything. **Nine pipettes attested three ways:** r04 (Ivy), r21 (Oram, who
53	handled the crate — "nine of them left in it at the end"), r22 (Falke, 1959, "the nine surviving
54	pipettes"). r19's "eleven" is one of its three transposition errors.
55	r22 adds physical confirmation: the pipettes "delivered materially less than the capacity blown upon
56	their stems, **and in the same proportion, one to another**."
57	
58	**(b) The true average test, and the shortfall in points.**

## Section A — Reconstruction (first three of the eight stories)

### 1. A creamery of their own, and one sentence in the by-laws (1889–1892)

In 1889 the farmers of the Larrow Valley met — in the schoolhouse, in cold weather, as Dell Rundle's
jubilee pamphlet (r12) has it — and organized the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association.
**Gideon Vose** was elected its first president and held the office **1889–1911**, twenty-two years,
longer than any other man (r02, Effie Loomis, secretary 1901–1940, writing from the minute book);
he **died in 1917**. The churn was set up at **Larrow Green in 1891**. In the same year the
Association was organized, **Ansel Keddie married Orra Brant (1889)** — a private fact that would
matter more than any other by 1925.

Gideon Vose wrote the by-laws in his own hand, **Article VII** among them. His son Selby said so in
print in 1926 (r08): "My father, who was your first president and who wrote the by-law under which
every patron in this Association is paid on the test of the station where he delivers." The
operative clause — transcribed verbatim by two independent hands, Loomis from the minutes (r02) and
Rundle (r12) — made **the test of the station where a man delivered govern his pay**. No appeal, no
second test, no reference to any other station's figure.

**When Article VII was adopted cannot be settled.** Loomis says **1892**; Rundle **1891**; Nyle
Grigg in 1919, flagging it as hearsay, **1893**. The printed by-laws carry no year on their face,
only "adopted at the annual meeting" (r07, Nym's accession notes), and the **1889–1892 minute book
was lost in the office move of 1938**. Orin Falke, writing in 195]
